The zero field method is a numerical-analytical method that belongs to the group of so-called numerical-analytical methods of diffraction theory.
The characteristic feature of the zero field method is the use of boundary conditions on a contour that differs from the scatterer contour.
The application of similar methods has been quite widespread in recent publications.

The paper presents a generalization of the zero field method to solve problems of the propagation of fields from point sources (electric or magnetic current filaments) in plane-layered media with two-dimensional inhomogeneities.

The paper proposes an algorithm for modeling the propagation of ultra-wideband pulsed signals in flat-layered media with cylindrical inclusions, based on expanding the original signals in Fourier series.
The results of the work are reflected in two regulatory documents: R V. 2.3-218-02071168-781:2011 and M 218-02071168-705:2012.
The paper's main focus is on rigorously justifying the application of the reduction method to the systems of linear algebraic equations that arise from the zero field method.

The key conclusion is that the numerical-analytical methods of modern electrodynamics, such as the zero field method, are effective tools for solving important applied problems, including non-destructive testing.
The paper notes that many questions still remain unanswered regarding the justification of the convergence of the zero field method.

The paper applies a traditional method of moments algorithm, rather than relying on the expansion of the Green's function in cylindrical waves, in order to justify the application of the reduction method.
The paper shows that the spectral coefficients and the derivatives of the Green's function with respect to the radial and angular coordinates of the source point are bounded functions.
The zero field method can be used to model the propagation and diffraction of both harmonic and ultra-wideband electromagnetic signals on objects of various shapes and electrical properties.

The methods presented in the paper can be used for non-destructive testing and quality control of industrial dielectric products, as well as for metrological support of measurement processes using defectometric complexes.
The paper suggests that the ideas for further improvement of the zero field method can be proposed as a perspective for further research in this direction.

The zero field method is characterized by the use of boundary conditions on a contour that differs from the scatterer contour, which is a distinctive feature of this class of numerical-analytical methods.
